newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania detergent maker seeks Henkel deal.
newsitem.headline: Romania detergent maker seeks Henkel deal.

text.p: A Romanian detergent maker said on Thursday it was hoping to strike a joint venture deal with Austria's Henkel Gruppe as the sole way to survive in a local market dominated by imports.

"Local output is just a tiny fraction of the detergent market, which is flooded with imports. The only solution is to associate with a foreign partner," Adalcisa Matulea, general manager of Apollo SA detergent maker, told Reuters from the Danube port town of Galati, where the company is based.
"If the deal comes through, Helkel will buy 51 percent and will also invest in re-equipping the plant," Matulea said.

Henkel Romania SRL, Henkel Austria Gruppe's subsidiary in Bucharest, confirmed talks were in progress for the acquisition of the 51 percent stake. "Our talks with the State Ownership Fund (FPS) are in a very advanced stage," Andreas Fuhrmann, manager of Helkel Romania, told Reuters.
The FPS is the present 51 percent shareholder of Apollo, which has a share capital of 4.6 billion lei.

Details of how much Henkel would pay for the stake were not available. But Matulea said Apollo needed a rough 9.0 billion lei for re-equipment by the year 2000. Fuhrmann said "several million dollars will be invested in Apollo".
Apollo already has a cooperation contract with Henkel to produce a monthly 200 tonnes of Rex-brand detergents for the domestic market.

Apollo, founded 120 years ago -- the year Henkel itself was set up -- has seen its output decline in recent years from monthly peaks of around 700 tonnes before the communists were ousted in 1989 to a present 70 tonnes. "We had a market at that time, as there were no imports," Matulea said.
If Apollo and Henkel join hands they will be competing in the Romanian market with Procter & Gamble Co and Anglo-Dutch Unilever Plc/NV, which already acquired one Romanian detergent maker each.
Detergent consumption in Romania is of some 60,000 tonnes, of which around 40,000 tonnes are imports, Fuhrmann said. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
